title: bug: VS Code AgentLauncher lets terminal control characters through to sendText (bash path unchecked)
description: moe-vscode/src/util/AgentLauncher.ts buildBashCommand never calls assertSafeArg, and assertSafeArg (PowerShell path) refuses only CR/LF/NUL. terminal.sendText types each char into the shell line editor, so a team name (= project.name from the repo-tracked .moe/project.json, extension.ts getTeamName) such as "x\u0015touch /tmp/pwned #" erases the typed quoting with Ctrl-U and runs the rest when a team-mode agent starts. Fix: refuse every C0 control and DEL on both paths (as VSC-15's accounts CLI line does); check JetBrains TerminalAgentLauncher for the same class. Found during VSC-15 (task-357ed3ae) self-review.
definitionOfDone: Both buildBashCommand and buildPowerShellCommand refuse any value containing U+0000..U+001F or U+007F, with a test per path that fails on HEAD.
JetBrains TerminalAgentLauncher's agent and accounts command lines are checked for the same class, and fixed or explicitly ruled safe with evidence.

implementationPlan.description:
JetBrains first (DoD 2): the agent and accounts builders refuse every C0 control and DEL.
In TerminalAgentLauncher.kt, next to psQuote/shQuote, add one private helper with a one-line why-comment:
  private fun requireSafeArg(label: String, value: String) =
      require(value.none { it < '\u0020' || it == '\u007f' }) { "Invalid $label: contains control characters" }
Why: every word is typed into the shell's line editor. writeToTtyConnector writes command + "\n" to the PTY. CR/LF end the line, and Ctrl-U (0x15) or Ctrl-W (0x17) erase the quoting typed before them, so the rest of the value would run (mem:gotcha-vscode-sendtext-control-chars).
Use exactly this rule. Do not use Character.isISOControl: it also refuses U+0080..U+009F, so it would disagree with VS Code's AgentLauncher and AccountsTreeProvider.
- buildPowerShellCommand and buildBashCommand: call it first, before any quoting, in this order: the script path ('script path'), basePath ('project path'), workerId ('worker id'), agentCommand ('command'), teamName when non-null ('team name'), then each env value ('env $key').
- The WSL routes need nothing more. buildWslBashCommand ends in buildBashCommand (toWslPath keeps a mid-value control character), and the .ps1-under-WSL route wraps buildPowerShellCommand's output in bashWrapPowerShell.
- buildAccountsCommand: before `when (shell)`, check every word of listOf(cli.node, cli.script, registryFile) + args, raw (before toWslPath), with the label 'accounts command word' (VSC-15's label in VS Code). All three AccountsShell values then refuse.
Tests, appended to TerminalAgentLauncherTest.kt (org.junit.Assert.assertThrows, JUnit 4.13.2):
(a) Agent lines. BAD = 0x00, 0x01, 0x09, 0x0A, 0x0D, 0x15, 0x17, 0x1B, 0x1F, 0x7F. Cover each code, each buildCommandForTest route — (POWERSHELL, wslAgents=false), (BASH, false), (BASH, true), (POWERSHELL, true) — and each carrier: basePath, scriptPath, agentCommand, teamName, workerId and one env value. Each must throw IllegalArgumentException whose message equals "Invalid <label>: contains control characters". Put the character mid-value ("D:/p<c>q"): toWslPath's regex `$` drops a TRAILING line terminator, so a trailing \n would never reach the WSL check.
(b) Accounts lines. For each code, each AccountsShell entry and each carrier (cli.node, cli.script, registryFile, one arg), the message is "Invalid accounts command word: contains control characters".
(c) Boundary. Values holding ' ', '~' and 'é' (U+0020, U+007E, U+00E9) still build on all four agent routes and on the three accounts shells. Assert the team argument verbatim: -Team 'a ~é' on the PowerShell routes, --team 'a ~é' on the bash routes.
Every existing test stays unchanged and green: none feeds a control character to a builder, and the agentCommandFor trim rows test a different function.
This step's error handling: the builders throw IllegalArgumentException and never catch it. Step 2 makes every caller show it before any tab opens.
implementationPlan.note: TerminalAgentLauncher.kt: private requireSafeArg (rule `it < ' ' || it == '\u007f'`, message "Invalid $label: contains control characters"), plus a private requireSafeLaunchArgs that checks script path, project path, worker id, command, team name (when non-null) and each env value, in the plan's order. It is the first line of both buildPowerShellCommand (script.absolutePath) and buildBashCommand. The plan asked for one helper; I added the second so both builders share one 6-check call instead of repeating 6 lines (mirrors VS Code's assertSafeLaunchArgs). buildAccountsCommand checks every raw word of listOf(node, script, registryFile) + args before `when (shell)`, labelled 'accounts command word'. Tests appended to TerminalAgentLauncherTest: (a) 10 codes x 4 routes x 6 carriers with exact messages, bad char mid-value; (b) 10 codes x 3 shells x 4 carriers; (c) 'a ~é' in every carrier builds on all routes and shells, with -Team 'a ~é' / --team 'a ~é' verbatim. Compile and run are deferred to step 4's gate. Dirty peer paths (.moe/roles, .moe/skills, scripts/moe-agent.*, scripts/tests/postflight*, peer .moe/tasks) were left untouched.

implementationPlan.description:
JetBrains callers refuse before any terminal tab opens, and tell the person (DoD 2).
(1) TerminalAgentLauncher.launchRole: for a Launch decision, compute teamName, workerId and the buildCommand(...) line first, inside the existing try and before openSeat. A Refused decision still builds nothing (keep the existing comment's contract). A refused value then lands in the existing catch, which shows "Failed to start terminal \"<tab>\": Invalid team name: contains control characters", and no tab is created. openSeat, sendCommand and trackSeat stay unchanged.
(2) runAccountsCommand: build `val line = accountsCommandLine(project, cli, registryFile, args)` first, before resolveTerminalManager and createTerminalWidget, and send `line`. Add to its KDoc that it throws IllegalArgumentException, before any tab opens, for a word with a control character.
(3) AccountsPanel.runCli: wrap the runAccountsCommand call and the clipboard fallback in try/catch (ex: IllegalArgumentException), and show Messages.showErrorDialog(project, "Account action failed: ${ex.message}", "Moe"). That is the text VS Code's AccountsTreeProvider.runCli shows. A refused line is never copied to the clipboard. Catch only IllegalArgumentException.
These edits need IntelliJ's Project and Messages, so no unit test reaches them. Step 1's tests prove the builders throw, and step 5 reviews these three edits by reading.
This step's error handling: every refusal produces exactly one dialog and no tab. startAgents shows one dialog per role, matching VS Code's one error per role.
implementationPlan.note: launchRole: for a non-Refused decision, teamName, workerId and buildCommand(...) are now computed first inside the existing try, before openSeat, as `launch: Pair<workerId, command>?`. A builder refusal lands in the existing catch ("Failed to start terminal \"<tab>\": Invalid <label>: contains control characters"), and no tab opens. A Refused decision still builds nothing: launch is null, openSeat shows its one dialog, and `if (launch == null) return`. openSeat, sendCommand and trackSeat are unchanged. runAccountsCommand builds `line` before resolveTerminalManager and createTerminalWidget, and its KDoc names the throw. AccountsPanel.runCli: the runAccountsCommand call and the fallback accountsCommandLine are in a try that catches only IllegalArgumentException and shows "Account action failed: ${ex.message}" (VS Code's text). It returns before CopyPasteManager, so a refused line is never copied. No unit test reaches these IntelliJ-bound callers. Step 5 reviews them by reading.

implementationPlan.description:
VS Code (DoD 1). moe-vscode/src/util/AgentLauncher.ts:
- assertSafeArg refuses `code < 0x20 || code === 0x7f`. Keep the charCodeAt loop and the message `Invalid ${label}: contains control characters`. Use no regex (mem:gotcha-vscode-eslint-no-control-regex). Rewrite its comment: sendText types each character into the line editor, where Ctrl-U or Ctrl-W erase the quoting typed before them. The -EncodedCommand base64 is typed too, so the decoded words are checked before encoding (mem:gotcha-vscode-sendtext-control-chars).
- Add a private `assertSafeLaunchArgs(scriptPath, workspacePath, workerId, command, envOverrides, teamName)`. It checks, in this order: 'script path', 'workspace path', 'worker id', 'command', 'team name' when set, then `env ${key}` for each value.
- Make it the first line of BOTH buildPowerShellCommand (replacing the inline checks and the check inside the env loop) and buildBashCommand. Add no export.
- Do not reuse this file's isControl (line 149). It masks U+0080..U+009F for display, so it would disagree with AccountsTreeProvider's rule.
- launchRole needs no change: both builders run before createTerminal, so the throw reaches the existing catch. That gives one `Failed to launch <role> agent: Invalid <label>: contains control characters`, no terminal, and onLaunched is never called.
New moe-vscode/tests/agent-launcher-controls.test.cjs (test files share no helper module):
- Copy agent-seats.test.cjs's harness: run/transpile, loadClient, tempDir/write/project/extension, decode and loadLauncher.
- Give loadLauncher a platform, and pass `process: Object.create(process, { platform: { value: platform } })` in run()'s globals, so both builders run on every host (CI runs ubuntu, windows and macos).
- Keep passing the test realm's Error (mem:gotcha-vscode-launcher-vm-realm-error), and await every launchAgent.
The tests:
- B1 (platform 'linux', the bash path) and P1 (platform 'win32', the PowerShell path), one test each. Cover each code in 0x00, 0x01, 0x09, 0x0A, 0x0D, 0x15, 0x17, 0x1B, 0x1F, 0x7F and each carrier:
  - teamName 'a<c>b';
  - provider 'custom' with customCommand 'my-cli<c>x';
  - the workspace fsPath: a path under os.tmpdir() that is never created. Exclude NUL here: Node's fs refuses a NUL path, the profile then reads as untrusted, and an earlier protected-runtime message wins.
  For each, launchAgent('architect', ...) creates no terminal, never calls onLaunched, and errors deep-equals [`Failed to launch architect agent: Invalid <label>: contains control characters`].
- E1: an extension() whose directory name holds \u0015, and one holding \u007f, is refused as 'script path' on both platforms, with no terminal. Skip it with a reason on win32 hosts (NTFS refuses these names), or wherever the mkdir throws.
- OK1: teamName 'a ~é' launches on both platforms, with one terminal and no error. The sent line holds --team 'a ~é' (bash), or -Team 'a ~é' after decoding (PowerShell).
This step's error handling: every refusal is exactly one error message and zero terminals, and nothing is typed.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1) Validate once in launchRole, before the platform branch. Rejected: the DoD names both builders, and per-builder checks also guard any future caller.
2) Reuse AgentLauncher's isControl, or Kotlin's Character.isISOControl. Rejected: both also refuse U+0080..U+009F, so the three typing sites would disagree; the DoD and VSC-15 name C0+DEL.
3) Rule JetBrains safe instead of fixing it. Rejected for three reasons:
- its team name is the IDE project name, which a repo-tracked .idea/.name can set;
- under LEGACY, settings.agentCommand comes unchanged from the repo-tracked .moe/project.json;
- account ids reach the line unvalidated: VSC-15's Q1 row feeds 'acct-2\ntouch /tmp/x' through the wire.
4) Export the VS Code builders and test them directly. Rejected: the black-box launchAgent test also proves that no terminal opens and that onLaunched is never called.
5) Fold in the PowerShell curly-quote and backtick injection found while planning (verified with benign probes on PowerShell 5.1). Rejected: it is a different class, outside this DoD and the 5-file cap. Filed as task-2f4b224f9afe47b4a5e382d5da7bb16c (BACKLOG, depends on this row and VSC-15).
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- Each plugin types into a terminal from exactly two places.
  - VS Code: AgentLauncher.launchRole, and AccountsTreeProvider.runCli (already fixed by VSC-15).
  - JetBrains: launchRole and runAccountsCommand, both through sendCommand -> writeToTtyConnector, which writes command + \n as UTF-8 bytes.
- VS Code's PowerShell path base64-encodes the inner script, and that base64 is itself typed with sendText. The decoded words must therefore be checked before encoding.
- The vscode test harness transpiles src into node:vm with closed require maps. process is a vm global, so a test can override the platform. Error is the vm realm's unless the test passes its own.
- buildCommandForTest drives all four JetBrains agent routes, including WSL bash and bashWrapPowerShell, with an explicit workerId.
planningNotes.risks:
- toWslPath's regex `$` drops a trailing line terminator: 'D:/p\n' becomes '/mnt/d/p'. Put the bad character mid-value in the Kotlin tests.
- A NUL in a fake VS Code workspace path makes Node's fs throw ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE. declaredProfile then reads 'untrusted', runtimeProfile 'protected', and a different refusal wins. Keep NUL out of the workspace-path rows.
- NTFS cannot hold control-character directory names, so skip E1 there. CI's windows job still runs B1, P1 and OK1.
- startAgents and launchAllAgents show one error per role for a bad project name: four in total, modal in JetBrains. This is accepted; no tabs or terminals open.
- A LEGACY agentCommand with stray control whitespace (for example 'claude\n' in project.json) is now refused. It produced a broken line before.
- C1 characters (U+0080..U+009F) stay allowed on purpose, as in VSC-15.
- The Gradle half of the chained checkRef must be proven to have run: :test not UP-TO-DATE, plus the XML counts.
